title: Rigveda 9.24: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.24: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.24 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 677r-677v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.24.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 677r
translation.original_text:
1pra somā̍so adhanviṣu̱ḥ pava̍mānāsa̱ inda̍vaḥ | śrī̱ṇā̱nā a̱psu mṛ̍ñjata ||
2a̱bhi gāvo̍ adhanviṣu̱r āpo̱ na pra̱vatā̍ ya̱tīḥ | pu̱nā̱nā indra̍m āśata ||
translation.text:
1HITHERWARD have the Soma streamed, the drops while they are purified: When blent, in waters they are rinsed.
2The milk hath run to meet them like floods rushing down a precipice: They come to Indra, being cleansed.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 677r (numbered 99r by the scribe) (OPenn image 677, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.22.7 ‹gavyāni dhārayaḥ tatam tantum›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 677v (numbered 99v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.24.3 ‹nṛ-bhiḥ yataḥ vi nīyase›. Verses 9.24.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pra | somāsaḥ | adhanviṣuḥ | pavamānāsaḥ | indavaḥ | śrīṇānāḥ | ap-su | mṛñjata
2abhi | gāvaḥ | adhanviṣuḥ | āpaḥ | na | pra-vatā | yatīḥ | punānāḥ | indram | āśata

translation.original_ref: RV 9.24.3-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 677v
translation.original_text:
3pra pa̍vamāna dhanvasi̱ somendrā̍ya̱ pāta̍ve | nṛbhi̍r ya̱to vi nī̍yase ||
4tvaṁ so̍ma nṛ̱māda̍na̱ḥ pava̍sva carṣaṇī̱sahe̍ | sasni̱r yo a̍nu̱mādya̍ḥ ||
5indo̱ yad adri̍bhiḥ su̱taḥ pa̱vitra̍m pari̱dhāva̍si | ara̱m indra̍sya̱ dhāmne̍ ||
6pava̍sva vṛtrahantamo̱kthebhi̍r anu̱mādya̍ḥ | śuci̍ḥ pāva̱ko adbhu̍taḥ ||
7śuci̍ḥ pāva̱ka u̍cyate̱ soma̍ḥ su̱tasya̱ madhva̍ḥ | de̱vā̱vīr a̍ghaśaṁsa̱hā ||
translation.text:
3O Soma Pavamâna, thou art flowing to be Indra's drink: The men have seized and lead thee forth.
4Victorious, to be hailed with joy, O Soma, flow, delighting men, To him who ruleth o'er mankind.
5Thou, Indu, when, effused by stones, thou runnest to the filter, art, Ready for Indra's high decree.
6Flow on, best Vr̥itra-slayer; flow meet to be hailed with joyful lauds. Pure, purifying, wonderful.
7Pure, purifying is he called the Soma of the meath effused, Slayer of sinners, dear to Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 677v (numbered 99v by the scribe) (OPenn image 678, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.24.3 ‹nṛ-bhiḥ yataḥ vi nīyase›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 678r (numbered 100r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.25.6 ‹-yonim āsadam›. Verses 9.24.3-7 end on this page; 9.24.3 begins on fol. 677r (numbered 99r by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
3pra | pavamāna | dhanvasi | soma | indrāya | pātave | nṛ-bhiḥ | yataḥ | vi | nīyase
4tvam | soma | nṛ-mādanaḥ | pavasva | carṣaṇi-sahe | sasniḥ | yaḥ | anu-mādyaḥ
5indo iti | yat | adri-bhiḥ | sutaḥ | pavitram | pari-dhāvasi | aram | indrasya | dhāmne
6pavasva | vṛtrahan-tama | ukthebhiḥ | anu-mādyaḥ | śuciḥ | pāvakaḥ | adbhutaḥ
7śuciḥ | pāvakaḥ | ucyate | somaḥ | sutasya | madhvaḥ | deva-avīḥ | aghaśaṃsa-hā
